sections.title: Nvidia stops selling H200 chips in China
paragraphs: Nvidia announced it will cease sales of its H200 accelerator chips in China following the board's decision to remove CEO Jensen Huang, a move reported on 20 November 2026[S1][S2]. The company released its latest earnings report the same week, showing continued revenue growth despite the leadership turmoil[S1].

The decision follows internal concerns about Huang's conduct, including alleged extramarital affairs and questions about candor that led to his ouster[S2]. Board members cited “multiple issues” and a year‑long pattern of lying as reasons for the leadership change[S2].

sections.title: Anthropic IPO tests safety‑first model
paragraphs: Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, completed an IPO on the Nasdaq last Thursday, becoming one of the most valuable companies on the planet[S3]. The filing shows the firm expects compute costs of roughly $900 billion over the coming years[S3]. The public listing raises questions about whether the company can keep prioritising safety while answering shareholder pressure[S3].

The IPO prospectus outlines a unique corporate‑governance structure designed to shield the firm from aggressive capitalist demands[S3]. Hayden Field notes that Anthropic’s pitch to large customers centres on its safety branding, which now sits in tension with profit motives[S3]. OpenAI’s decision to let Anthropic go public first is also discussed as a strategic move in the broader AI market[S3].
The tension between safety research and shareholder expectations is a recurring theme in the industry, highlighted by recent debates over governance at other AI firms[S3].

sections.title: Google Duplex added to Gemini tasks
paragraphs: Google introduced Duplex in 2018 to enable natural voice calls with local businesses and later integrated it into the Gemini app this week, allowing the AI to make reservations and other errands on a user's behalf[S4]. The feature now runs as part of Gemini Tasks, a personal AI collaborator that can place calls and handle real‑world requests[S4].

Duplex began as a narrow, closed‑domain system but has been rebuilt on the Gemini foundation model stack, combining speech understanding, contextual reasoning, and speech synthesis in a low‑latency pipeline[S4]. During the COVID‑19 pandemic the system added automatic merchant‑info verification, contributing data that appeared in Search and Maps over one trillion times by 2023[S4]. Since 2019 Google also moved parts of the model onto Pixel devices via Call Assist features[S4].

Duplex was created to address the difficulty of phone conversations that do not follow strict scripts, requiring the AI to handle interruptions, tone cues, and timing nuances[S4]. Its evolution reflects broader Google efforts to embed conversational AI across products such as Search and Maps, leveraging advances in large foundation models to deliver more seamless, real‑world assistance[S4].

sections.title: Nvidia stops H200 chip sales to China
paragraphs: Nvidia announced it will no longer sell its H200 AI chips to customers in China, according to interim CEO Colette Kress, and the decision was confirmed on the TechCrunch Equity podcast on 21 November 2026[S5].

The H200 chips were previously accessed by Chinese firms via data centres located in nearby countries such as Malaysia, allowing remote use of the hardware despite export bans[S5]. Nvidia publicly declared the shutdown of this arrangement, citing tighter restrictions from the Trump administration and ongoing limits under the Biden administration[S5]. Analysts estimate that roughly 20% of Nvidia's overall business is linked to China, though this figure is not reflected in direct sales numbers because the revenue comes through indirect channels[S5]. The company’s executives reassured investors that they have the situation under control, even as the stock price fell amid uncertainty[S5].
The restriction reflects broader geopolitical tension over AI technology and its strategic importance[S5].

sections.title: OpenAI upgrades safeguards against adversarial distillation
paragraphs: OpenAI announced updated defenses for its GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol models to block adversarial distillation, a technique where attackers copy model capabilities without permission[S6].

The new safeguards combine adversarial testing, specialized classifiers, and API‑level controls to detect and Disrupt attempts to extract protected reasoning[S6]. In an adaptive evaluation, attack success fell from 54.0% on the original GPT‑6 Astra to 0.2% on the upgraded GPT‑6.2 Astra, indicating a near‑complete block of chain‑of‑thought leakage[S6]. OpenAI also aligned these measures with protections used in biology and cybersecurity, emphasizing cross‑domain safety consistency[S6].

Adversarial distillation lets bad actors train a surrogate model using outputs and internal steps from a frontier AI, potentially bypassing safety filters[S6]. This risk extends beyond intellectual property, as the extracted reasoning can enable harmful actions such as cyberattacks that the original model would refuse[S6]. By strengthening defenses, OpenAI aims to set industry standards for preventing capability leakage while maintaining model usefulness[S6].
